$comment: THE hand-written part. Four packages -- ui, js, php, py -- are generated from this directory and are never edited. Every API fact here is read from Google's YouTube v3 discovery document (https://youtube.googleapis.com/$discovery/rest?version=v3).
title: YouTube

oauth.$refreshTokenRotates: Reusable. A refresh response carries access_token, expires_in, scope and token_type — no refresh_token — and Google’s own expiry rule is "the refresh token has not been used for six months", which is a statement about a token that is PERSISTED AND REPLAYED. Under rotation it would change hourly and that rule could never fire.
oauth.$grantComment: ONE consent grant shared by every Google connector (MOIC #1, 2026-11-08). A host may run them all on one OAuth client: request each feature's scopes when it is first used, with include_granted_scopes=true, and Google's new token covers every scope granted before. A refresh token comes back only on the FIRST code exchange with access_type=offline, so keep the stored one when an exchange returns none. Revoking ANY token removes the person's WHOLE grant -- every Google connector, not this one -- so a per-feature disconnect stops using the scope locally and only a full Google disconnect revokes. Identify the account by the id_token's sub (request openid; verify iss and aud = clientId), never by email.
oauth.$restrictedScopesComment: Google's RESTRICTED tier puts the whole OAuth client under verification and an annual CASA assessment. None of this connector's scopes is restricted.
oauth.$scopeComment: playlistItems.insert accepts youtube, youtube.force-ssl and youtubepartner. youtube.force-ssl is narrower than full `Manage your YouTube account` access while still allowing edits to videos and related channel resources, so it is the least authority this action needs; youtubepartner is for content partners.
oauth.$comment: The host performs the browser consent flow and refreshes Google's one-hour access token; refreshToken is required so the connection does not expire after that hour.

$sandboxComment: CHECKED. YouTube exposes no separate test estate. Adding a test video creates a real playlist item on a real YouTube channel.
sandboxNote: YouTube has no sandbox. Every live-mode add changes a real playlist; use the faker during development and remove live test items afterward.
